authorization: Root authorized one isolated future-probe capture utility and one small fabricated qualification; preserve all existing scientific sources and evidence.
question: Can an exclusive capture transaction preserve an independently written exact copy and durable identity record before dependent reads, while explicitly rejecting changed or lost evidence and duplicate writers?

transaction.reservation: Exclusive new directory and fsynced reservation before a child is started; one raw_probe.json writer only.
transaction.expected_identity: Incremental SHA256 and byte length from bytes successfully written by the capture writer, independent of later file hashing.
transaction.commit: Require a closed, fsynced, within-cap writer. Verify original against expected stream identity. Exclusively write a separate inode at objects/<sha256>.bin, fsync it and its directory, reverify original and copy, then exclusively write and fsync commit.json and its directory. Never overwrite or rename original capture.
transaction.dependent_read: Caller pins the returned commit identity. Verified read requires that exact commit, its bound reservation, and both original and object identities; return bytes only from the committed object. Missing or changed original/copy fails explicitly, with no silent fallback or scientific-status change.
transaction.partial_failure: Retain bounded original/partial object and reservation. No commit means no permission to consume. A failure is never relabeled as scientific success.
transaction.threat_and_durability_scope: Cooperating callers on the host filesystem. Exclusive creation prevents a second API writer; later unauthorized writes are detected at validation boundaries. Independent inodes and fsync improve survivability but do not prove physical storage independence, power-loss correctness, or resistance to an actor able to change all bytes and external bindings. The original capture-loss mechanism remains unattributed.

fixed_cases.name: exact_binary_commit
fixed_cases.check: One child, binary payload larger than buffer, precommit read rejection, distinct original/object inodes, exact committed read.

fixed_cases.name: legitimate_empty
fixed_cases.check: A deliberately empty stream can be committed and verified; expected stream identity distinguishes it from loss.

fixed_cases.name: duplicate_writers
fixed_cases.check: Second reservation, writer and commit all reject without changing committed bytes.

fixed_cases.name: original_truncated_after_commit
fixed_cases.check: Explicit injected truncation makes verified read fail; independent object survives.

fixed_cases.name: original_deleted_after_commit
fixed_cases.check: Explicit injected deletion makes verified read fail; independent object survives.

fixed_cases.name: object_corrupted_after_commit
fixed_cases.check: Explicit injected corruption makes verified read fail; original survives.

fixed_cases.name: original_truncated_before_commit
fixed_cases.check: Stream identity mismatch prevents commit; no dependent payload read.

fixed_cases.name: output_cap_exceeded
fixed_cases.check: Bounded partial output retained, child ended, over-cap writer cannot commit.

qualification_evidence: Preserve exact child commands, plan/module/qualification/Python identities, per-child exact wait4 resources, case assertions and explicitly injected corruptions, aggregate CPU/wall/RSS and closed-file manifest. No optional repeated qualification after the planned pass.
finish_line: One small saved qualification and independent static review. Integration into a future scientific probe requires that probe's own preflight/source binding; this utility does not alter any historical result or repair the failed autonomous invocation.
